chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna, from Abu Basir, who said: A man asked him (the Imam), and I was listening.
He said: Should I give my relatives from the zakat of my wealth, while they do not know you? He said: No, give the zakat only to a Muslim, and give them from your wealth other than the zakat.

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do you think that only zakat is in the wealth? What Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has obligated in the wealth other than zakat is more than what you give to your relatives and the casual passerby who asks you. So you give them while you do not know them by the 'Nasb' (sect), but if you know them by the 'Nasb', do not give them (zakat) unless you fear their tongue, so you buy your religion and your honor from them.

key_terms.النَّصْب: Al-Nasb (a term often referring to the early Sunni sects or those opposing the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Can I give my Zakat to my relatives who are not Muslim or are from the Nasb sect?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between *zakat* (obligatory alms) and *sadaqat* (voluntary charity), ruling that zakat is restricted to Muslims and excludes those of the *Nasb* sect unless fear of their tongue necessitates it for peace. He further emphasizes that the non-zakat financial dues owed to relatives and supplicants often exceed the zakat portion, highlighting the broader scope of wealth purification beyond the specific zakat category. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that zakat has stricter eligibility criteria than general charitable giving.
